Elaine: FYI I opened a docs PR that adds a short 'VPC NAT + HAProxy troubleshooting' appendix to private-deploy.md. Includes quick curl checks, nft/iptables snippets, a pod-level kubectl check, and a tiny Node SDK TLS-fallback example. Need review and a link sanity check.
Matt: Nice. Can you paste the snippets here? Also add a note about asymmetric SNAT behavior AWS vs GCP — people trip on that. :eyes:
Elaine: Snippets pasted below — tried to keep them minimal.
Elaine: ```bash
# HAProxy behind a NAT gateway - simple health check from jumpbox
curl -v -H "Host: apps.internal.redwood" http://10.0.5.12:8080/health

# Verify NAT/SNAT mappings on the node (nftables example)
sudo nft list table nat | grep -E "snat|masq" -A2

# Quick container-level check if service is reachable from pod
kubectl exec -n infra -it $(kubectl get pods -n infra -l app=jumpbox -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- curl -sS --connect-timeout 3 http://10.0.5.12:8080/health
```
Matt: Quick nit — for kube example prefer `-o jsonpath` with single quotes escaped like you used, but maybe include the simpler `kubectl run --rm -i --tty debug --image=curlimages/curl -- sh` pattern for folks without a jumpbox.
Jess: Also add a short 'what to look for in HAProxy logs' snippet — just one example line so people can grep.
Elaine: Good call. Adding this log sample and grep:
Elaine: ```
# HAProxy log example (syslog)
Apr 21 13:12:08 haproxy[1234]: 10.0.5.12:52344 [21/Apr/2026:13:12:08.123] http-in~ backend/app/0 200/0/-1/10/11 0/0 "GET /health HTTP/1.1"
# Grep for backend latency or 5xx spikes
grep "backend/app" /var/log/haproxy.log | tail -n 50
```
Diego: Content looks solid. One more thing — the link to /docs/private/network/ports.md is currently returning 404 in the rendered site. CI link checker flagged it. Can you point to /docs/networking/ports-reference.md instead?
docs-bot: Link check: broken links found in PR #423 (private-deploy.md): [/docs/private/network/ports.md] -> 404. See https://ci.redwood.internal/links/423 for details.
Elaine: Thanks — will update to the /docs/networking/ports-reference.md target and push a tiny follow-up commit. Also adding a one-liner about 'HSM outbound' ports and how to test egress to hardware HSM appliances (tcp/16963 common, confirm with vendor).
Matt: For SDK examples can you include a minimal Node snippet that shows using a local TLS-fallback proxy (dev only)? Helps platform teams reproduce TLS handshake fallbacks quickly.
Elaine: Added this Node example to the appendix:```js
// dev-only TLS-fallback proxy example (do not use in prod)
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference-sdk');
const client = new Redwood({ baseUrl: 'https://localhost:8443', tls: { rejectUnauthorized: false } });
(async () => {
  try {
    const r = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1', prompt: 'ping' });
    console.log('ok', r.text);
  } catch (e) {
    console.error('proxy test failed', e.message);
  }
})();
```
Jess: Could you also add a tiny troubleshooting table? Symptom -> quick check -> expected? That saves triage time.
Elaine: Added a 3-row table (latency spikes, 502/504, service unreachable) with one-liner checks and example log greps.
Diego: LGTM from a content standpoint. Please ensure the PR description mentions 'CI link fix included' so the reviewer knows one commit fixes the broken link.
Matt: I'll run a quick proofread and the link-check job locally. If green I'll approve and merge. :thumbsup:
Elaine: Thanks — pushed the link fix and the extra snippets. CI is queued.

Elaine: Fantastic, thanks everyone :rocket:
